clues: This town stands where two rivers meet and join as one. The joined stream flows on past farms and hills.
Winters here are warmer than in the rest of the state, because this city sits west of the high land. It has four clear seasons.
A new state split off from an old one in war time. For years the top job bounced from town to town, till it stayed here in 1885.
Salt made this city rich in its early days. The first salt well here was drilled in 1806, after rich salt brines were found along the river.
The governor of West Virginia works in this town, the biggest in the whole state. Its lawmakers meet in the state house, right by the river.
